parameters.title: Chemometric chain of spectral pre-processes
parameters.label: Run a chain of spectral pre-processing steps (filter, scatter correction, derivative, variable scaling, variance threshold, ward clustering, PCA) in one go and save the result with the suffixes and preprocessing chain of all steps; the result is the same as running the steps one by one.

parameter.hint: The root fp of the project
The dataframe to use as input, raw = original spectra, previous = the latest saved parquet file(s), or state the name of the parquet file with spectra derived from earlier step(s) to use as input.

Steps applied in the listed order. Each item is a method name with default settings: moving-average, gauss, savitzky-golay, lowess (filters), l1, l2, max, snv, msc (scatter correction), derivative (1st), meancentring, autoscaling, paretoscaling, poissonscaling (variable scaling), pca (5 components); or an object with custom settings: {"filter": <set name, JSON path or settings>}, {"multi_filter": ...}, {"scatter_correction": ["snv","snv"]}, {"derivative": 2}, {"scaling": "autoscaling"}, {"variance_threshold": {"threshold": 0.03, "scaler": "minmax"}}, {"ward_clustering": {"n_clusters": 40, "connectivity": true}} (n_clusters required), {"pca": 5}.

Instead of chemometrics_array: run the pre-processing chain recorded in the companion JSON of a saved dataframe, given as a dataframe name in project_root_fp or a path relative to the project root (.json optional), e.g. 1350-2500_10.snv.sg5.d1.mc.wc40.pca5. The input dataframe must have the same spectral range and resolution.
Optional user extension (1-6 letters, digits or -) added to the file suffix after a hashtag, e.g. .ma5#12321, to tell apart outputs with settings the suffix does not show.
Colour ramp for plotting spectra: a matplotlib colormap name, or default = the spectra_plot parameter set (ml_setting, "jet").

parameters.title: Convert spectra to derivatives
parameters.label: Convert spectra to derivatives and either append to or replace the original bands in the dataframe; with dataframe_array, compare the derivatives of several preprocessed dataframes and select one interactively.

parameter.hint: The root fp of the project
The dataframe to use as input, raw = original spectra, previous = the latest saved parquet file(s), or state the name of the parquet file with spectra derived from earlier step(s) to use as input.

Compare mode: two or more input dataframes (raw, previous or parquet file names, .parquet optional), e.g. raw and the outputs of different preprocessing pipelines. The derivative of every input is plotted and you choose which one to save. Overrides dataframe.
Derivative to calculate from the input dataframe.

if append is set to true the derivatives will be appended to the original bands; this is not recommended but can be used to explore which is more significant, the orignal bands or the derivatives, and then iterated to only select one for the coninued modeling.
Colour ramp for plotting spectra: a matplotlib colormap name, or default = the spectra_plot parameter set (ml_setting, "jet").

parameters.title: Scatter correction of spectral data
parameters.label: Run a single or a sequence of scatter corrections. Scatter correction works per spectrum and removes additive and multiplicative effects of light scattering (particle size, packing, path length).

parameter.hint: The root fp of the project
The dataframe to use as input, raw = original spectra, previous = the latest saved parquet file(s), or state the name of the parquet file with spectra derived from earlier step(s) to use as input.
Scatter correction, or array of 2 to apply in sequence. Available options: l1, l2, max, snv, msc; or select = plot all and choose interactively which one to apply.
Colour ramp for plotting spectra: a matplotlib colormap name, or default = the spectra_plot parameter set (ml_setting, "jet").

parameters.title: Variable scaling of spectral data
parameters.label: Run a variable scaling: every band (variable) is centred and/or scaled across all samples, to balance the influence of the bands in the modelling.

parameter.hint: The root fp of the project
The dataframe to use as input, raw = original spectra, previous = the latest saved parquet file(s), or state the name of the parquet file with spectra derived from earlier step(s) to use as input.
Available options: meancentring, autoscaling, paretoscaling, poissonscaling; or select = plot all and choose interactively which one to apply.
Colour ramp for plotting spectra: a matplotlib colormap name, or default = the spectra_plot parameter set (ml_setting, "jet").

parameters.title: Decomposition of spectral data
parameters.label: Run a decomposition for compressing the information of spectral signals; with dataframe_array, compare the decomposition of several preprocessed dataframes and select one interactively.

parameter.hint: The root fp of the project
The dataframe to use as input, raw = original spectra, previous = the latest saved parquet file(s), or state the name of the parquet file with spectra derived from earlier step(s) to use as input.

Compare mode: two or more input dataframes (raw, previous or parquet file names, .parquet optional), e.g. raw and the outputs of different preprocessing pipelines. The decomposition of every input is plotted with its explained variance and you choose which one to save. Overrides dataframe.
Available options: Principal Component Analysis (pca).
Available options: Pricipal Component Analysis (pca).
Colour ramp for plotting spectra: a matplotlib colormap name, or default = the spectra_plot parameter set (ml_setting, "jet").
